score: 72 recommendations: 65 judged and agreeing with the original on the dataset, 7 not judged, 0 observed wrong; none estimated 2% cheaper; 2 ran at least 1.4x faster
metric: KumoSQL's recommended rewrites (the rule pipeline and the proof-gated optimizer) on 103 TPC-DS and 53 DSB statements, judged in a fixed order: correctness first (proof label, then same rows when executed against the original), then the EXPLAIN cost estimate, then measured runtime, each reported on its own.
correctness: No wrong result observed under the stricter comparison (rows as a bag with multiplicity, output column names and types, sort keys including hidden ones, floats to 9 places), on one workload (PostgreSQL scale factor 1, seed 7, rerun 2026-10-03): 65 of 72 recommendations were judged by the row comparator and agreed with the original; 7 rule rewrites were not judged because the original no longer runs on PostgreSQL after the BigQuery round trip the rules need. Proof and dataset agreement are separate facts: 66 of the 72 carry a proof; 6 are unproven (CTE inlining around window functions), of which 5 ran and returned the same rows and 1 (q21) was not judged. Agreement on one dataset is evidence, not a proof, and a proof holds only under its stated assumptions
coverage_of: The 72 recommended rewrites from the 156 statements, by proof label: 66 carry a proof, 6 are labelled unproven.
usefulness: Rules: 44 recommendations (27 parenthesis removals, 24 single-use CTE inlinings), all estimated unchanged and none 10% faster or slower; they simplify text, not plans. Optimizer: 28 recommendations, none estimated at least 2% cheaper; two ran faster at an essentially unchanged estimate (TPC-DS q38 1.40x, q87 1.42x), none slower by 10%, so on this draw the estimate predicted no saving and missed two
performance: Median of 5 alternating runs after a warm-up on PostgreSQL 16, TPC-DS and DSB at scale factor 1; geometric-mean speedup 1.001x (rules, 37 judged) and 1.017x (optimizer, 28)
caveats: What "0 wrong" covers: 44 rule and 28 optimizer recommendations on 103 TPC-DS and 53 DSB statements; it excludes build recommendations, shared-model proposals, cost attribution and change reports. The proof holds under its model (declared keys and NOT NULL hold, floats are never NaN, runtime errors are not modeled, rows tied under ORDER BY or LIMIT may be chosen differently), and the optimizer accepts a rewrite whose estimate is up to 2% higher, so accepted does not mean cheaper. These assumptions are copied into every record the tool writes. This run used the stricter comparator, which appends hidden sort keys and compares output column names and types; floats still compare rounded to 9 decimal places (differences below about 5e-10 are invisible) and agreement on one dataset can never rule out a looser predicate that agrees on the data (WHERE k = 10 against k < 15). The queries were regenerated for this run (TPC-DS templates with the Netezza dialect file, DSB's PostgreSQL templates, dsqgen seed 7, 103 + 53 statements) and are not stored in the repo (TPC licence); the first run's query text was not kept, so this is a fresh draw from the same templates and the two runs' estimates and timings differ (the first run's one estimated saving, DSB query069, did not recur). No held-out split. Estimates are PostgreSQL EXPLAIN costs, a local stand-in for BigQuery dry-run bytes; no real BigQuery run yet. In the first run one optimizer rewrite (TPC-DS q44) compared as different rows because tied rows came back in another order; the comparison now allows ties in any order.
